correctness.rationale: Both curves scale by a^(1−t)b^t, so separate determinant-one normalization preserves the ordering. Cayley–Hamilton yields M=(A⁻¹+B)/K and N=(A⁻¹+D)/K, with determinants one and tr(AM)=tr(AN)=K>0. In a unitary eigenbasis of A, pairing the ij and ji terms in tr(D)−tr(B) yields the squared commutator sum; it vanishes exactly when A commutes with B^(1/2), equivalently with B. Thus the rapidities satisfy v≥u, strictly when AB≠BA. The two-point interpolation of T^(2t) on e^(±w) gives the displayed two-term trace difference, valid by continuity also at w=0. Strict increase of x coth x gives decreasing sinh(pw)/sinh(w) for 0<p<1 and increasing for p>1. The two coefficients of the trace difference thus have the same sign in the open intervals. At t=1 the first term is zero, not strictly increasing as stated for the combined range in Step 4; the F_2 term alone gives strictness. Both terms yield zero difference at t=0 and t=1/2. Equal positive determinants make largest eigenvalue strictly increasing with trace, giving the claimed spectral comparisons, not a Löwner-order claim.
residual_risks: The finite rational checks do not certify arbitrary complex inputs or all t; those are covered by the proof. The Step 4 wording about both terms being strictly increasing needs the endpoint qualification above. No assertion in higher dimensions follows.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the uniform sign on the open intervals on both sides of the midpoint for arbitrary complex positive-definite 2×2 inputs, together with the trace defect and strictness in the noncommuting case. Ibrahim–Huang state this range comparison as a conjecture, supply the near-curve normal form, and establish weak endpoint ordering and midpoint isospectrality; the latter facts are not new here. No inspected source establishes the dimension-two interval sign comparison or a result implying it without the new trace sign analysis.

value.rationale: Dimension two is the first matrix dimension with a nontrivial log-majorization condition. Resolving the proposed comparison there for every positive-definite pair, and identifying strictness through a commutator defect, explains exactly how the two curves separate across their known isospectral midpoint. This is more than recovery of the known endpoint or of special finite examples.
residual_risks: The reduction to one trace inequality is specific to dimension two; no higher-dimensional proof or Löwner-order statement is implied.
